purpose: Finite adapter-boundary controls for carrier and policy assumptions.
common_known_nonclaims: This evaluation does not produce a canonical SOFRS, SOFAUDIT, or SOFAction artifact.
No fixture establishes adapter scientific adequacy or domain truth.
No fixture establishes mixing time, rank collapse, Lie/Hall depth, action selection, authorization, execution, outcome, or causal effect.

fixtures.strongest_claim: For this finite exact-rational nonnegative single-letter operator, every declared off-diagonal support-graph path agrees with positive matrix-power support and the recomputed first-hit census.
known_nonclaims: The result is not a mixing-time claim.
The result is not route depth, rank collapse, or Lie/Hall depth.
The graph equivalence is not declared for signed, complex, or multi-letter systems.

fixtures.strongest_claim: The union support graph contains two length-two routes from 0 to 2, while the signed matrix square has entry (0,2)=0 because the route contributions cancel.
known_nonclaims: Union-graph reachability is not positive matrix-power support in this signed regime.
No route-depth or word-depth promotion is made.
The signed matrix is not admitted as an exact-rational Markov source.

fixtures.strongest_claim: The unlabelled union graph has path 0->1->2, but selected word AA has zero (0,2) support; labelled word AB is the separate control with nonzero (0,2) support.
known_nonclaims: Union-graph reachability does not determine a selected labelled word.
No multi-letter closure or exact depth theorem is asserted.
No canonical word carrier is created by this fixture.

fixtures.strongest_claim: Under cutoff d_max=2, pair 0->3 is recorded as UNREACHED_AT_CUTOFF while the finite depths 0->1=1 and 0->2=2 are observed.
known_nonclaims: The cutoff does not establish nonexistence of a later path.
No exact word-depth or saturation claim is made beyond the declared cutoff.

fixtures.strongest_claim: For the declared strict-greater-than threshold rule, the finite support count changes across the supplied threshold sweep and is therefore threshold-relative.
known_nonclaims: The sweep does not identify a scientifically privileged threshold.
Near-threshold support is not a stable domain fact without a declared numerical policy.
No tolerance-independent equivalence or adequacy claim is made.
